questions.chapter: Chapter 2: Discrete Fourier Transform & Properties, Circular Convolution
questions.text: Define Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) ($X[k] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] W_N^{kn}$) and Inverse DFT. State properties of DFT: Linearity, Periodicity, Circular Time Shift, Circular Frequency Shift, and Parseval's Theorem. Explain Circular Convolution ($x_1[n] \mathbin{\circledast} x_2[n]$) and show how Linear Convolution is computed via DFT and IDFT with zero padding.

questions.chapter: Chapter 1: Discrete-Time Signals, Systems & Frequency-Domain Characterization
questions.text: Derive the Radix-2 Decimation-in-Time (DIT-FFT) butterfly algorithm. Show how the computational complexity is reduced from $O(N^2)$ complex multiplications to $O(N \log_2 N)$. Draw the complete 8-point DIT-FFT butterfly signal flow graph (Bit-reversal order input to natural order output) and calculate the 8-point DFT for $x[n] = \{1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1\}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Infinite Impulse Response Filter Design
questions.text: Explain the design of Analog Butterworth Lowpass Filter (Magnitude response $|H(j\Omega)|^2 = \frac{1}{1 + (\Omega/\Omega_c)^{2N}}$, order determination $N \ge \frac{\log_{10}\left(\frac{10^{0.1\alpha_s}-1}{10^{0.1\alpha_p}-1}\right)}{2\log_{10}(\Omega_s/\Omega_p)}$, and pole distribution on s-plane). Design an analog Butterworth filter to satisfy passband ripple $\le 1\,\text{dB}$ at $\Omega_p = 20\,\text{rad/s}$ and stopband attenuation $\ge 30\,\text{dB}$ at $\Omega_s = 50\,\text{rad/s}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Infinite Impulse Response Filter Design
questions.text: Explain Bilinear Transformation (BLT) ($s = \frac{2}{T}\frac{1-z^{-1}}{1+z^{-1}}$) for transforming analog filters into digital IIR filters. What is Frequency Warping ($\Omega = \frac{2}{T}\tan\frac{\omega}{2}$) and how is pre-warping used to eliminate warping error? Convert an analog filter $H_a(s) = \frac{2}{s+2}$ into a digital IIR filter $H(z)$ using BLT with $T = 0.5\,\text{s}$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 5: Infinite Impulse Response Filter Design
questions.text: Explain Linear Phase characteristics of FIR filters (Symmetric and Antisymmetric impulse response $h[n] = \pm h[M-1-n]$ for constant phase delay and group delay). What are the four types of linear phase FIR filters and their zero locations at $z = 1, -1$?

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Finite Impulse Response Filter Design
questions.text: Design a digital FIR Lowpass Filter of length $M = 7$ ($N = 6$) with cutoff frequency $\omega_c = 0.4\pi\,\text{rad/sample}$ using: (a) Rectangular Window, and (b) Hamming Window ($w[n] = 0.54 - 0.46\cos\frac{2\pi n}{M-1}$). Compute filter coefficients $h[n]$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Finite Impulse Response Filter Design
questions.text: Explain Multirate Digital Signal Processing: (a) Decimation (Downsampling by integer factor $M$ and anti-aliasing filter), (b) Interpolation (Upsampling by integer factor $L$ and anti-imaging filter), and (c) Sampling Rate Conversion by rational factor $I/D$.

questions.chapter: Chapter 4: Finite Impulse Response Filter Design
questions.text: Explain Overlap-Add Method and Overlap-Save Method for linear filtering of long duration data sequences using DFT.
Derive the Radix-2 Decimation-in-Frequency (DIF-FFT) algorithm. Draw the 8-point DIF-FFT butterfly flow graph (Natural order input to bit-reversal order output) and compare DIT vs DIF algorithms.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: Digital Filter Structures & Finite Word-Length Effects
questions.text: Explain Finite Wordlength Effects in digital filters: (a) Input quantization noise, (b) Coefficient quantization error and pole sensitivity, (c) Roundoff noise in multipliers, and (d) Limit cycle oscillations (Zero-input limit cycles and Overflow limit cycles).
